items.text: Pro-étale schemes
$X$ over $k$ is pro-étale if $X=\varprojlim X_i$ (filtering) with $X_i$ finite étale.
$X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine pro-étale $\iff$ $A=\varinjlim A_i$, $A_i$ finite étale over $k$ (products of finite separable extensions) $\iff$ $A$ integral and separable over $k$.
This descends: $X$ affine pro-étale over $k$ iff $X_{k'}$ is over $k'$ (descent: a property true after a faithfully flat base change was true before).
$k$ separably closed: affine pro-étale $k$-schemes $\simeq$ compact totally disconnected spaces,
X\longmapsto X(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(A,k)=\varprojlim\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,k)\quad(\text{inverse-limit topology})
Pro-category of finite sets $\simeq$ compact totally disconnected spaces. Inverse: a space with the sheaf of locally constant functions to $k$.
Locally profinite schemes
Every point has a neighbourhood affine pro-étale (contains both étale and affine pro-étale schemes); underlying spaces locally compact.

For $X$ quasi-compact (say) there is a locally profinite scheme $\underline\pi_0(X/k)$ and a morphism $X\to\underline\pi_0(X/k)$, universal for morphisms of $X$ into locally profinite schemes, surjective with geometrically connected fibres; stable under base change and products.
For a group scheme $G$: $G/G^0:=\underline\pi_0(G/k)$ (profinite in general, discrete if $G$ locally of finite type).
Exercise: in a quasi-compact scheme the connected component of $x$ is the intersection of all open and closed subsets containing $x$.
Geometric regularity

Fact (algebra, EGA). $k$ perfect, $X$ a regular scheme over $k$, $k'/k$ a field extension. If $X$ is essentially locally of finite type over $k$ or $k'$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ (so the local rings of $X_{k'}$ are noetherian), then $X_{k'}$ is regular.
Essentially of finite type: $A\simeq S^{-1}B$ with $B$ of finite type over $k$; for a field extension: finitely generated as a field.
Proposition. $k$ any field, $X$ essentially locally of finite type over $k$, $k_1$ a perfect extension of $k$. Equivalent:
(a) for every regular $k$-scheme $Y$, $X\times_kY$ is regular;
(b) for every extension $k'/k$, $X_{k'}$ is regular;
(c) $X_{k_1}$ is regular;
(d) for every finite extension $k'/k$, $X_{k'}$ is regular.
Definition: such an $X$ is geometrically regular; smooth over $k$ = locally of finite type and geometrically regular.
Proof. (a)$\Rightarrow$(b),(c),(d) trivial ($Y=\operatorname{Spec}$ of a field).
(b)$\Rightarrow$(a): $A\to B$ local homomorphism of local rings of $Y$ and $X\times Y$; $A$ regular, $B$ flat over $A$, and $B/\mathfrak mB$ regular (by (b), the fibre over $\kappa(y)$).
Claim. $A\to B$ local, noetherian, $B$ flat over $A$, $A$ and $B/\mathfrak mB$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $B$ regular.

\mathfrak m_A=(x_1,\dots,x_n),\ (x_i)\ A\text{-regular}\ \Rightarrow\ (x_i)\ B\text{-regular (flatness)};\quad B/(x_i)=B/\mathfrak mB\ \text{regular, so extend by a regular sequence ending at }\mathfrak m_B
(c)$\Rightarrow$(b): take $k'_1$ a composite of $k_1$ and $k'$; $X_{k'_1}$ is regular (base change of $X_{k_1}$ over the perfect field $k_1$); descend to $X_{k'}$ using:
Flat descent of regularity. $A\to B$ local, noetherian, $B$ flat over $A$, $B$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $A$ regular (global dimension; Serre, Auslander–Buchsbaum).
(d)$\Rightarrow$(c): take $k_1$ the perfect closure; $X_{k_i}$ regular for finite $k_i$, so $X_{k_1}$ regular by passage to the limit.
